revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Patio Pavers
revealWordProblem.text: Claire's architecture firm is laying pavers on a parallelogram-shaped patio for a client. The patio has a base of 16 feet and a perpendicular height of 9 feet. The slanted side of the patio measures 11 feet. Each box of pavers covers 12 square feet. How many full boxes of pavers should Claire order to cover the entire patio?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: First find the area: A = base × height = 16 × 9 = 144 square feet (the 11 ft slanted side is not used). Then divide by the box coverage: 144 ÷ 12 = 12 boxes. Claire should order 12 boxes of pavers.

conceptIntro.heading: How do we find the area of a parallelogram?
conceptIntro.intro: A parallelogram is a four-sided shape with two pairs of parallel sides, like a leaning rectangle. Its area is how much flat space is inside it.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Area of Parallelograms & Rhombuses. Formula: Area = Base × Height (A = b · h). 1. Identify the base (any side). 2. Identify the perpendicular height (height must be perpendicular to base, not slanted). 3. Multiply base times height; label with square units (e.g. cm², in²)

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: I have a parallelogram with a base of 14 feet and a height of 9 feet.
I write the formula: A = base × height.
I put in the numbers: A = 14 × 9.
So the area is 126 square feet. I used the height of 9, not the slanted side.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Now a smaller parallelogram: base = 5 cm, height = 4 cm.
What is the formula? A = base × height.
What do we put in? A = 5 × 4.
What is 5 × 4? Yes, 20, so the area is 20 square centimeters.

youDo.title: Now it's your turn
lines: Next you will plot the patio on a grid and find its area yourself.
Remember: multiply the base by the height, and always use the perpendicular height.

discourse.prompt: If you cut a triangle from one side of the parallelogram and move it to the other side, what shape do you get? How does this help you find the area?
discourse.sentenceFrame: The area of the parallelogram equals base x height = ___ x ___ = ___ square feet, which is the same as a ___ with the same base and height.

optional.stem: Cut the slanted end off a parallelogram and slide it to the other side. What shape forms, and why does that show A = base × height?
choices: A rectangle with the same base and height, so its area equals base x height
A bigger parallelogram, so the area gets larger
A triangle, so the area is cut in half
A square, so all four sides must be equal
optional.explanation: Sliding the cut triangle turns the parallelogram into a rectangle that keeps the same base and height. A rectangle's area is base x height, so the parallelogram's area is base x height too.
choiceFeedback: Does cutting and moving a piece change how much space is covered?
The rearranged shape still has the same area as before.
After rearranging, do you have three sides or four?
optional.stemEs: Corta el extremo inclinado de un paralelogramo y deslízalo al otro lado. ¿Qué figura se forma y por qué eso muestra que A = base × altura?
optional.explanationEs: Deslizar el triángulo cortado convierte el paralelogramo en un rectángulo que conserva la misma base y la misma altura. El área de un rectángulo es base × altura, así que el área del paralelogramo también es base × altura.
hints: Cutting a piece off and sliding it somewhere else moves the surface around but does not add or remove any of it.
Picture the new outline after the triangle slides over: think about whether the corners become square.
The base along the bottom never changes, and the straight-up height never changes either. Ask yourself which familiar shape has those exact two measurements and square corners.
hintsEs: Cortar una parte y deslizarla a otro lugar mueve la superficie, pero no añade ni quita nada de ella.
Imagina el nuevo contorno después de deslizar el triángulo: piensa si las esquinas quedan rectas.
La base de abajo no cambia, y la altura vertical tampoco cambia. Pregúntate qué figura conocida tiene esas dos medidas exactas y esquinas rectas.
choicesEs: Un rectángulo con la misma base y la misma altura, así que su área es igual a base × altura
Un paralelogramo más grande, así que el área aumenta
Un triángulo, así que el área se reduce a la mitad
Un cuadrado, así que los cuatro lados deben ser iguales

optional.stem: A blueprint parallelogram has a base of 8 ft, a height of 5 ft, and a slanted side of 7 ft. What is its area?
optional.explanation: Area = base x height = 8 x 5 = 40 sq ft. The 7 ft slanted side is not used; only the perpendicular height belongs in the formula.
choiceFeedback: Use the perpendicular height (5 ft), not the slant side (7 ft).
Height times slant is not the formula; use base times height.
Which measurement is perpendicular to the base?
optional.stemEs: Un paralelogramo de un plano tiene una base de 8 ft, una altura de 5 ft y un lado inclinado de 7 ft. ¿Cuál es su área?
optional.explanationEs: Área = base × altura = 8 × 5 = 40 pies cuadrados. El lado inclinado de 7 ft no se usa; solo la altura perpendicular entra en la fórmula.
hints: Not every measurement in a problem belongs in the formula — area only needs a base and its perpendicular height.
Identify which of the three numbers describes the straight-up distance, then leave the slanted side out entirely.
The base is 8 ft and the perpendicular height is 5 ft. Multiply those two and label the result in square feet.
hintsEs: No toda medida de un problema pertenece a la fórmula: el área solo necesita una base y su altura perpendicular.
Identifica cuál de los tres números describe la distancia vertical y deja el lado inclinado completamente fuera.
La base es 8 ft y la altura perpendicular es 5 ft. Multiplica esas dos y etiqueta el resultado en pies cuadrados.

optional.instructions: Each label describes a segment on a parallelogram blueprint. Sort each one into 'Is the height' or 'Is NOT the height'.

items.text: A dashed line straight up from the base, making a 90 degree angle
items.textEs: Una línea punteada recta hacia arriba desde la base, formando un ángulo de 90 grados

items.text: The slanted left edge of the parallelogram
items.textEs: El lado izquierdo inclinado del paralelogramo

items.text: The perpendicular distance from the base to the top side
items.textEs: La distancia perpendicular desde la base hasta el lado superior

items.text: The long tilted side that connects the bottom to the top
items.textEs: El lado largo inclinado que conecta la parte de abajo con la de arriba

items.text: The straight-up distance measured at a right angle to the base
items.textEs: La distancia vertical medida en ángulo recto con la base

items.text: The leaning side that is longer than the perpendicular gap
items.textEs: El lado inclinado que es más largo que la distancia perpendicular

optional.hint: Check which measurements are straight-up (perpendicular) to the base.
optional.explanation: The three cards that mention a 90 degree angle, a perpendicular distance, or a straight-up measurement to the top all describe the height. The slanted left edge, the long tilted side, and the leaning side longer than the perpendicular gap are sides of the figure, not the height — a slanted segment is always longer than the true straight-up distance.
optional.explanationEs: Las tres tarjetas que mencionan un ángulo de 90 grados, una distancia perpendicular o una medida vertical hasta la parte de arriba describen la altura. El borde izquierdo inclinado, el lado largo ladeado y el lado inclinado más largo que la separación perpendicular son lados de la figura, no la altura: un segmento inclinado siempre es más largo que la distancia vertical real.
optional.instructionsEs: Cada etiqueta describe un segmento en el plano de un paralelogramo. Clasifica cada una en 'Es la altura' o 'NO es la altura'.

optional.label: Match each parallelogram's base and height to its correct area (A = base x height).
optional.hint: Multiply base x height for each pair to find the area.
optional.explanation: Multiply base by height on each card: 6 × 7 = 42 sq ft, 13 × 2 = 26 sq ft, 4 × 11 = 44 sq ft, and 15 × 4 = 60 sq ft. Notice 6 × 7 and 4 × 11 give close totals, so read both numbers carefully before you commit to a match.
optional.explanationEs: Multiplica base por altura en cada tarjeta: 6 × 7 = 42 sq ft, 13 × 2 = 26 sq ft, 4 × 11 = 44 sq ft y 15 × 4 = 60 sq ft. Fíjate en que 6 × 7 y 4 × 11 dan totales parecidos, así que lee bien los dos números antes de decidir la pareja.
optional.labelEs: Une la base y la altura de cada paralelogramo con su área correcta (A = base × altura).

optional.stem: Two parallelograms both have base 10 ft and height 6 ft. N is more tilted (slant 9 ft). Compare their areas.
choices: Equal: both are 10 x 6 = 60 sq ft because area depends on base and height, not the slant
Blueprint N is larger because its slanted side is 9 ft
Blueprint M is larger because it is less tilted
You cannot compare them without the slanted side of M
optional.explanation: Area = base x height. Both have base 10 ft and height 6 ft, so both areas are 10 x 6 = 60 sq ft. Tilting the shape changes the slanted side but not the perpendicular height, so the area stays the same.
choiceFeedback: If base and height do not change, does area change?
Tilting the shape changes the slant, not the perpendicular height.
Does the formula A = base x height depend on the slant?
optional.stemEs: Dos paralelogramos tienen base 10 ft y altura 6 ft. N está más inclinado (lado inclinado de 9 ft). Compara sus áreas.
optional.explanationEs: Área = base × altura. Ambos tienen base 10 ft y altura 6 ft, así que ambas áreas son 10 × 6 = 60 pies cuadrados. Inclinar la figura cambia el lado inclinado, pero no la altura perpendicular, así que el área se mantiene igual.
hints: The area formula only takes in two measurements: the base and the perpendicular height.
Check whether either of those two measurements is different between the shapes before deciding anything about tilt.
Both shapes report base 10 ft and height 6 ft, so run 10 × 6 for each one and see what that tells you about the comparison.
hintsEs: La fórmula del área solo usa dos medidas: la base y la altura perpendicular.
Revisa si alguna de esas dos medidas es distinta entre las figuras antes de decidir algo sobre la inclinación.
Ambas figuras tienen base 10 ft y altura 6 ft, así que calcula 10 × 6 para cada una y observa qué te dice esa comparación.
choicesEs: Iguales: los dos son 10 × 6 = 60 pies cuadrados, porque el área depende de la base y la altura, no de la inclinación
El plano N es más grande porque su lado inclinado mide 9 pies
El plano M es más grande porque está menos inclinado
No se pueden comparar sin el lado inclinado de M

optional.correctWork: The height is 7 ft, not the slanted side of 10 ft. Substitute the perpendicular height: A = 12 x 7 = 84 sq ft. Only the straight-up height belongs in A = base x height.

The height must be perpendicular (a 90 degree angle) to the base. The 10 ft slanted side is not the height, so use 7 ft instead.
optional.titleEs: Extensión Nivel 2 — El desliz del lado inclinado
optional.explanation: The blueprint lists three numbers, and the substitution step grabs the 10 ft slanted side instead of the 7 ft height. Since A = base × height only accepts the perpendicular measurement, the real area is A = 12 × 7 = 84 sq ft.
optional.explanationEs: El plano da tres números, y el paso de sustitución toma el lado inclinado de 10 ft en lugar de la altura de 7 ft. Como A = base × altura solo acepta la medida perpendicular, el área real es A = 12 × 7 = 84 sq ft.

hintsEs: Mira el paso de sustitución. ¿Qué número usó el diseñador para la altura — el lado inclinado o la altura real?

approaching.stem: What is the area of a parallelogram with base 10 cm and height 7 cm?
choiceFeedback: Did you add? The formula multiplies base and height.
You found 10 + 7; try multiplying instead.
That label measures a distance along a line, but area describes the flat region a shape covers. Multiplying two lengths always produces square units.
hints: You know both the base (10 cm) and the height (7 cm) — this is a direct use of the parallelogram area formula.
Area of a parallelogram is A = base × height. Adding the two numbers gives perimeter-style thinking, not area.
Set up A = 10 × 7 and multiply. Label your result in square centimeters.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de un paralelogramo con base 10 cm y altura 7 cm?
hintsEs: Conoces tanto la base (10 cm) como la altura (7 cm): este es un uso directo de la fórmula del área del paralelogramo.
El área de un paralelogramo es A = base × altura. Sumar los dos números es pensar en perímetro, no en área.
Plantea A = 10 × 7 y multiplica. Escribe tu resultado en centímetros cuadrados.

approaching.stem: A parallelogram has an area of 54 sq ft and a base of 9 ft. What is the height?
choiceFeedback: Work backwards: if A = b × h and A = 54, h = 54 ÷ 9.
54 + 9 is too large for the height.
Is the height half of 54?
hints: This time you're given the area (54 sq ft) and the base (9 ft) — the height is the missing piece.
Start from A = b × h. To undo a multiplication, divide: h = A ÷ b.
Write 54 = 9 × h, then divide 54 by 9 to find the height in feet.
approaching.stemEs: Un paralelogramo tiene un área de 54 pies cuadrados y una base de 9 ft. ¿Cuál es la altura?
hintsEs: Esta vez te dan el área (54 pies²) y la base (9 pies): la altura es la pieza que falta.
Empieza con A = b × h. Para deshacer una multiplicación, divide: h = A ÷ b.
Escribe 54 = 9 × h y luego divide 54 entre 9 para hallar la altura en pies.

approaching.stem: What is the area of a parallelogram with base 9 cm and height 5 cm?
choiceFeedback: Add base and height? The formula multiplies them.
You added 9 + 5; try multiplying.
22.5 is half of 45; is that the area formula?
hints: Spot the base (9 cm) and the height (5 cm). Which operation does the area formula use on them?
Use A = base × height. If your number looks like 9 + 5, or like half the product, rethink the operation.
Compute 9 × 5 and give the answer in square centimeters.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de un paralelogramo con base 9 cm y altura 5 cm?
hintsEs: Identifica la base (9 cm) y la altura (5 cm). ¿Qué operación usa la fórmula del área con ellas?
Usa A = base × altura. Si tu número se parece a 9 + 5, o a la mitad del producto, repiensa la operación.
Calcula 9 × 5 y da la respuesta en centímetros cuadrados.

approaching.stem: Which measurement is the height of a parallelogram?
choices: The perpendicular distance between the base and the opposite side
The length of the slanted side
approaching.explanation: The height is always the perpendicular (straight up-and-down) distance between the base and the opposite side, not the slanted side.
choiceFeedback: The slanted side is not perpendicular to the base.
Perimeter is around the shape; height is perpendicular distance.
The longest side is not always the height.
hints: Picture a leaning parallelogram. The height is not a side you can trace — it's a distance measured straight across.
Height must make a right angle (90°) with the base. Test each choice: is this perpendicular to the base?
Draw a base, then a straight up-and-down dashed line to the opposite side. That dashed line is what 'height' means here.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál medida es la altura de un paralelogramo?
approaching.explanationEs: La altura siempre es la distancia perpendicular (recta, de arriba abajo) entre la base y el lado opuesto, no el lado inclinado.
choicesEs: La distancia perpendicular entre la base y el lado opuesto
hintsEs: Imagina un paralelogramo inclinado. La altura no es un lado que puedas trazar: es una distancia medida en línea recta.
La altura debe formar un ángulo recto (90°) con la base. Prueba cada opción: ¿es perpendicular a la base?
Dibuja una base y luego una línea punteada recta hacia arriba hasta el lado opuesto. Esa línea punteada es lo que significa 'altura' aquí.

approaching.instructions: Use the formula A = b × h to find the area of each parallelogram.
approaching.hint: For each row, multiply base x height to find the missing area.
hints: Each row gives a base and a height in feet — the empty Area column is what you fill in.
Use A = b × h for every row, and write the unit as sq ft since feet × feet gives square feet.
Start with Patio X: multiply 6 × 4. Then do Patio Y the same way with 11 × 3.
approaching.explanation: Each row already gives a base and a perpendicular height, so A = b × h finishes it: Patio X is 6 × 4 = 24 sq ft and Patio Y is 11 × 3 = 33 sq ft. Feet times feet gives square feet, which is why the area column carries sq ft.
approaching.explanationEs: Cada fila ya te da una base y una altura perpendicular, así que A = b × h lo resuelve: el Patio X da 6 × 4 = 24 sq ft y el Patio Y da 11 × 3 = 33 sq ft. Pies por pies da pies cuadrados, por eso la columna de área lleva sq ft.
approaching.instructionsEs: Usa la fórmula A = b × h para encontrar el área de cada paralelogramo.
hintsEs: Cada fila da una base y una altura en pies; la columna vacía de Área es la que llenas tú.
Usa A = b × h en cada fila y escribe la unidad como pies² porque pies × pies da pies cuadrados.
Empieza con el Patio X: multiplica 6 × 4. Luego haz el Patio Y igual con 11 × 3.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake
approaching.correctWork: Area uses multiplication, not addition. The formula is A = base × height, so A = 7 × 4 = 28 sq ft.
hints: Look at the substitution step. Did the student add the base and height, or multiply them?
The area formula multiplies the base and height: A = 7 × 4 = 28 sq ft, not 7 + 4.
approaching.explanation: The formula line is written correctly, but the substitution step turns A = base × height into A = 7 + 4. Area counts the squares that cover the shape, so you multiply: A = 7 × 4 = 28 sq ft.
approaching.explanationEs: La línea de la fórmula está bien escrita, pero el paso de sustitución convierte A = base × altura en A = 7 + 4. El área cuenta los cuadrados que cubren la figura, así que se multiplica: A = 7 × 4 = 28 sq ft.
approaching.correctWorkEs: El área usa multiplicación, no suma. La fórmula es A = base × altura, así que A = 7 × 4 = 28 pies cuadrados.
hintsEs: Mira el paso de sustitución. ¿El estudiante sumó la base y la altura, o las multiplicó?
La fórmula del área multiplica la base y la altura: A = 7 × 4 = 28 pies cuadrados, no 7 + 4.

onLevel.hint: Use A = b x h to find area; use h = A / b to find missing height.
hints: Check each row: Patios A and D are missing area, but Patios B and C are missing a base or a height.
Missing area → multiply b × h. Missing base or height → divide the area by the measurement you know.
For Patio B: 56 = 8 × h, so divide 56 by 8. For Patio A, multiply 14 × 9.
onLevel.explanation: Patios A and D give both measurements, so multiply: 14 × 9 = 126 sq ft and 15 × 6 = 90 sq ft. Patios B and C give the area and one measurement, so divide to undo the multiplication: 56 ÷ 8 = 7 ft of height and 96 ÷ 12 = 8 ft of base.
onLevel.explanationEs: Los Patios A y D dan las dos medidas, así que multiplicas: 14 × 9 = 126 sq ft y 15 × 6 = 90 sq ft. Los Patios B y C dan el área y una medida, así que divides para deshacer la multiplicación: 56 ÷ 8 = 7 ft de altura y 96 ÷ 12 = 8 ft de base.
hintsEs: Revisa cada fila: a los Patios A y D les falta el área, pero a los Patios B y C les falta una base o una altura.
Falta el área → multiplica b × h. Falta la base o la altura → divide el área entre la medida que sí conoces.
Para el Patio B: 56 = 8 × h, así que divide 56 entre 8. Para el Patio A, multiplica 14 × 9.

onLevel.label: Match each shape to its area.
onLevel.hint: Compute each area using base and height values in the formula.
hints: Read each shape's name first — triangles follow a different rule than parallelograms, rectangles, and squares.
Parallelograms, rectangles, and squares: multiply the two numbers. Triangles: multiply, then take half.
Try 'Triangle 8×6' first: take half of 8 × 6. Then 'Parallelogram 5×4' is just 5 × 4.
onLevel.explanation: The shape name decides the rule. Parallelogram 5×4 = 20, Rectangle 7×3 = 21, Square side 6 = 36, and Parallelogram 9×2 = 18 all just multiply, while the triangles take half: Triangle 8×6 = 24 and Triangle 10×8 = 40.
onLevel.explanationEs: El nombre de la figura decide la regla. Paralelogramo 5×4 = 20, Rectángulo 7×3 = 21, Cuadrado de lado 6 = 36 y Paralelogramo 9×2 = 18 solo multiplican, mientras que los triángulos toman la mitad: Triángulo 8×6 = 24 y Triángulo 10×8 = 40.
onLevel.labelEs: Une cada figura con su área.
hintsEs: Lee primero el nombre de cada figura: los triángulos siguen una regla distinta a la de paralelogramos, rectángulos y cuadrados.
Paralelogramos, rectángulos y cuadrados: multiplica los dos números. Triángulos: multiplica y luego saca la mitad.
Prueba primero 'Triángulo 8×6': saca la mitad de 8 × 6. Luego 'Paralelogramo 5×4' es solo 5 × 4.

onLevel.instructions: Sort each parallelogram by whether its area is greater than 50 sq units or 50 or less.
onLevel.hint: Calculate area first, then sort by comparing the results.
hints: Each card gives you a base and a height. Find the area first — area of a parallelogram is base × height — then compare that area to 50.
'Greater than 50' means strictly more than 50. An area of exactly 50 belongs in the '50 or less' group.
First card: b = 12, h = 5 gives A = 60. Ask: is 60 more than 50? Place it, then repeat for every card.
onLevel.explanation: Each card already shows its area, so you compare it to 50: 60, 80, and 77 are greater than 50, while 42, 36, and 50 are not. The card b = 5, h = 10 lands on exactly 50, and since 'greater than' means strictly more, it belongs in the 'Area ≤ 50 sq units' group.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada tarjeta ya muestra su área, así que la comparas con 50: 60, 80 y 77 son mayores que 50, mientras que 42, 36 y 50 no lo son. La tarjeta b = 5, h = 10 cae exactamente en 50, y como «mayor que» significa estrictamente más, va en el grupo «Área ≤ 50 unidades cuadradas».
onLevel.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada paralelogramo según si su área es mayor que 50 unidades cuadradas o 50 o menos.
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta ya muestra su área después de la flecha: tu trabajo es comparar ese número con 50.
'Mayor que 50' significa estrictamente más de 50. Un área de exactamente 50 va en el grupo de '50 o menos'.
Primera tarjeta: b = 12, h = 5 da A = 60. Pregunta: ¿es 60 más que 50? Colócala y repite con cada tarjeta.

onLevel.instructions: A parallelogram has base 8 ft. Place a point on the number line at the height that gives an area of 48 sq ft. (Hint: A = b × h, so h = A ÷ b.)
onLevel.label: Find the missing height: b = 8, A = 48
onLevel.hint: Remember: height is perpendicular distance, not the slanted side.
hints: You're placing a point at the height, not the area. Use the base (8 ft) and the area (48 sq ft) to find it.
Rearrange A = b × h into h = A ÷ b to solve for the missing height.
Divide 48 by 8, then place your point at that value on the number line.
onLevel.explanation: You know the base is 8 ft and the area is 48 sq ft, so rearrange A = b × h into h = A ÷ b. That gives 48 ÷ 8 = 6, so the point belongs at 6 on the number line — a height of 6 ft.
onLevel.explanationEs: Sabes que la base es 8 ft y el área es 48 sq ft, así que reacomodas A = b × h como h = A ÷ b. Eso da 48 ÷ 8 = 6, por lo que el punto va en el 6 de la recta numérica: una altura de 6 ft.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the parallelogram
workedExample.work: base = 9 cm, slanted side = 10 cm, height = 6 cm
workedExample.workEs: base = 9 cm, lado inclinado = 10 cm, altura = 6 cm

onLevel.correctWork: The height is 6 cm, not the slanted side of 10 cm. Substitute the perpendicular height: A = 9 × 6 = 54 sq cm. Only the straight-up height belongs in A = base × height.
hints: Look at the substitution step. Which number was used for the height — the slanted side or the real height?
The height must be perpendicular (a 90° angle) to the base. The 10 cm slanted side is not the height, so use 6 cm: A = 9 × 6 = 54 sq cm.
onLevel.explanation: The substitution step uses 10 cm, which is the slanted side, instead of the 6 cm height listed in the first step. Only the perpendicular height belongs in A = base × height, so A = 9 × 6 = 54 sq cm.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso de sustitución usa 10 cm, que es el lado inclinado, en lugar de la altura de 6 cm que aparece en el primer paso. En A = base × altura solo entra la altura perpendicular, así que A = 9 × 6 = 54 sq cm.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: La altura es 6 cm, no el lado inclinado de 10 cm. Sustituye la altura perpendicular: A = 9 × 6 = 54 cm cuadrados. Solo la altura recta va en A = base × altura.
hintsEs: Mira el paso de sustitución. ¿Qué número se usó para la altura — el lado inclinado o la altura real?
La altura debe ser perpendicular (un ángulo de 90°) a la base. El lado inclinado de 10 cm no es la altura, así que usa 6 cm: A = 9 × 6 = 54 cm cuadrados.

extending.title: Find the Area Error

workedExample.label: Identify base and height
workedExample.work: b = 11 m, slant side = 8 m, h = 6 m
workedExample.labelEs: Identifica la base y la altura
workedExample.workEs: b = 11 m, lado inclinado = 8 m, h = 6 m

extending.correctWork: The height is 6 m, not the slant side of 8 m. A = 11 × 6 = 66 sq m. Always use the perpendicular height, not the slanted side.
hints: Look at Step 3. Which value should be used for h — the slant side or the height?
The height must be perpendicular to the base. The slant side is not the height.
extending.explanation: The Substitute step plugs in the 8 m slant side for h, but the first step already labeled the height as 6 m. The slant side is longer than the true straight-up distance, so the correct area is A = 11 × 6 = 66 sq m.
extending.explanationEs: El paso Sustituir mete el lado inclinado de 8 m como h, pero el primer paso ya había marcado la altura como 6 m. El lado inclinado es más largo que la distancia vertical real, así que el área correcta es A = 11 × 6 = 66 sq m.
extending.correctWorkEs: La altura es 6 m, no el lado inclinado de 8 m. A = 11 × 6 = 66 m cuadrados. Usa siempre la altura perpendicular, no el lado inclinado.
hintsEs: Mira el Paso 3. ¿Cuál valor debe usarse para h — el lado inclinado o la altura?
La altura debe ser perpendicular a la base. El lado inclinado no es la altura.

extending.prompt: A parallelogram has a base of 12 cm. If you double the height, the area doubles too. Explain why this happens using the formula, and give a specific example with numbers.
extending.sentenceFrame: When the height doubles from ___ to ___, the area changes from ___ to ___ because in the formula A = b × h, the base stays at ___ and ___.
extending.hint: Pick a starting height; use A = base x height to see what happens.
hints: The base stays 12 cm the whole time — only the height changes. Your explanation should lean on A = b × h.
Pick an easy starting height (like 5 cm), find the area, then double the height to 10 cm and find the new area.
Compute 12 × 5, then 12 × 10. Describe what happened to the area when the height doubled, using the word 'multiply'.
extending.explanation: In A = b × h the base of 12 cm is a fixed factor, so the area is just 12 times whatever the height is. With h = 5, A = 12 × 5 = 60 sq cm; doubling to h = 10 gives A = 12 × 10 = 120 sq cm, exactly double, because doubling one factor doubles the product.
extending.explanationEs: En A = b × h la base de 12 cm es un factor fijo, así que el área es simplemente 12 veces la altura que tengas. Con h = 5, A = 12 × 5 = 60 sq cm; al duplicar a h = 10 queda A = 12 × 10 = 120 sq cm, exactamente el doble, porque duplicar un factor duplica el producto.
extending.promptEs: Un paralelogramo tiene una base de 12 cm. Si duplicas la altura, el área también se duplica. Explica por qué pasa esto usando la fórmula y da un ejemplo específico con números.
hintsEs: La base se queda en 12 cm todo el tiempo; solo cambia la altura. Tu explicación debe apoyarse en A = b × h.
Escoge una altura inicial fácil (como 5 cm), halla el área, luego duplica la altura a 10 cm y halla el área nueva.
Calcula 12 × 5 y luego 12 × 10. Describe qué le pasó al área cuando la altura se duplicó, usando la palabra 'multiplicar'.

extending.instructions: Plot a parallelogram with base 10 and height 6 on the grid. Then calculate its area and compare it to the rectangle 10 × 6.
extending.label: Plot the parallelogram and find its area.
extending.hint: Plot the four points, then calculate area using A = base x height.
hints: The four targets A, B, C, D are the corners. The bottom runs from x = 0 to x = 10, and the top sits at y = 6.
The base is the length along the bottom; the height is the vertical distance up to the top — even though the sides slant.
Plot A(0,0), B(10,0), C(12,6), D(2,6). Then use A = base × height with base 10 and height 6, and compare to the 10 × 6 rectangle.
extending.explanation: Plotting A(0,0), B(10,0), C(12,6), D(2,6) makes a parallelogram whose bottom side is 10 units long and whose top sits 6 units up, so A = 10 × 6 = 60 square units. It equals the 10 × 6 rectangle because sliding the slanted triangle from one end to the other turns the parallelogram into that rectangle without gaining or losing area.
extending.explanationEs: Al marcar A(0,0), B(10,0), C(12,6), D(2,6) se forma un paralelogramo cuyo lado inferior mide 10 unidades y cuyo lado superior está 6 unidades arriba, así que A = 10 × 6 = 60 unidades cuadradas. Es igual al rectángulo de 10 × 6 porque, al mover el triángulo inclinado de un extremo al otro, el paralelogramo se convierte en ese rectángulo sin ganar ni perder área.

practice.commonMistake: The most common mistake in Area of Parallelograms is multiplying the base by the slanted side instead of the perpendicular height. For a parallelogram with a base of 16 ft, a perpendicular height of 9 ft, and a slanted side of 11 ft, students compute 16 × 11 = 176 square feet instead of the correct 16 × 9 = 144 square feet. The height must be the straight-up (perpendicular) distance between the base and its opposite side, not the length of the slanted side, even though the slanted side is often the number that 'looks' like it belongs in the formula.

connect.scenario: A landscape architect is tiling a parallelogram-shaped courtyard. The courtyard has a base of 18 feet and a height of 10 feet. Each tile covers 2 square feet.
connect.promptQuestion: How many tiles does the architect need?
connect.prompt: The courtyard's area is ___ sq ft because A = ___ x ___ . She needs ___ tiles because ___ / 2 = ___.

check.stem: What is the area of the parallelogram courtyard?
check.explanation: A = base × height = 18 × 10 = 180 sq ft. Use the perpendicular height, not a slanted side.

check.stem: How many tiles does the architect need?
check.explanation: Each tile covers 2 sq ft, so 180 ÷ 2 = 90 tiles.

check.stem: Why use the height instead of the slanted side length?
choices: Because area needs the perpendicular distance between the two bases
Because the slanted side is always longer
Because the base is on the bottom
check.explanation: Sliding the end triangle over turns a parallelogram into a rectangle whose sides are the base and the perpendicular height — that is why A = b × h.

connect.modelAnswer: A = base × height = 18 × 10 = 180 sq ft. Each tile covers 2 sq ft, so the architect needs 180 ÷ 2 = 90 tiles. Use the perpendicular height (10 ft), not a slanted side.

exitTicket.stem: A parallelogram has a base of 13 inches and a height of 5 inches. What is its area?
exitTicket.explanation: A = b x h = 13 x 5 = 65 square inches.
choiceFeedback: Area of a parallelogram is base × height, not adding sides.
That looks like base + height — multiply them instead.
Right number, wrong unit — area is measured in square inches.
hints: You have a base of 13 inches and a height of 5 inches — both numbers the parallelogram formula needs.
Use A = b × h, and remember area is measured in square inches, not plain inches.
Multiply 13 × 5 (try 10 × 5 plus 3 × 5) and label the result in square inches.
